answer: According to the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, wrongful restraint is defined as voluntarily obstructing a person to prevent them from proceeding in any direction they have a right to go (Section 126(1)). In contrast, wrongful confinement occurs when a person is wrongfully restrained in such a manner that they cannot proceed beyond certain circumscribing limits (Section 127(1)). The penalties for wrongful restraint can include simple imprisonment for up to one month or a fine of up to five thousand rupees (Section 126(2)). Wrongful confinement, while not explicitly detailed in the provided evidence, is implied to carry more severe penalties, especially if grievous hurt is caused (Section 125(b)).
summary_answer: Wrongful restraint involves preventing a person from proceeding in any direction they have a right to go, while wrongful confinement restricts a person within certain limits.
